text:
Carter Verhaeghe has 10 goals and 21 points in 23 games, the kind of steady scoring line Florida has come to expect from a three-time Cup winner. Underneath it, our numbers see the biggest luck flag on the Panthers. Florida has scored 12.1 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that is padding his total. On-ice luck like that fades.

His own work holds up better. He has 7.95 expected goals (the quality of his chances), 1.13 per 60 minutes, comfortably above last season's 0.94. Ten goals on that is a little hot, at 20.4% shooting, but not wildly so. The last ten games brought eight assists and only two goals, including a three-assist night against Detroit.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season shows a complete player: 72% of his exits leave the zone with possession, and his 9.7 primary shot assists per 60 rank in the 93rd percentile among forwards. Evolving-Hockey said his team created more with him on the ice, against competition in the 94th percentile. The scoring may slow; the player is real.
headline: Verhaeghe's points are running ahead of his line
